summary: Draft review lays out an email the agent wrote the way the email will go: who it is to, the subject, the message and what is attached. People can edit it, then send it now, schedule it from a dropdown beside Send, or discard it. A warning can stop it before it goes, like a message that mentions an attachment when nothing is attached, and after sending there is a short window to undo.
use: When the agent writes on someone's behalf and nothing should leave without them seeing it.
When people want to change a word or two before it goes, not write it again.
When some messages are better sent later, like at the start of the reader's day.
When a check can catch a mistake before sending, and a sent message can still be taken back for a few seconds.
features: `to` shows each recipient as a chip with an avatar. `subject` sits in a plain input, and `body` stays editable; read edits from `onBodyChange`.
`attachments` show as file chips, with a spinner in place of the size while one is `loading`.
`warning` folds open above the buttons with its own actions, like Send anyway and Attach the summary.
The dropdown beside Send picks when it goes. `sendOptions` replace the defaults (now, tomorrow at 09:00, Monday at 09:00), and any pick but `now` turns the button into Schedule.
`phase` moves from `draft` to `sending`, then `undo`, `sent`, `scheduled` or `discarded`. The tag in the header follows it, and the fields dim while it is out of your hands.
In the `undo` phase a green row counts down `undoLeft` with an Undo button. A scheduled message can be cancelled and a discarded draft brought back, all through `onUndo`.
a11y: The subject is a labelled input and the message is a multi-line textbox labelled "Message".
The dropdown button is labelled "When to send" and says whether its menu is open. Each time is a menu item that marks the picked one with `aria-checked`, and Escape closes the menu.
Once it is sent, scheduled or discarded, the fields are inert, so they can't be edited or reached with Tab until it is undone.

faq.a: No. It calls `onSend` with the picked option and shows the `phase` you pass. Your code sends or schedules the message, runs the undo window and moves the phase along.

faq.q: Does it check for missing attachments by itself?
faq.a: No. The preview checks whether the message mentions an attachment when nothing is attached, and passes a `warning`. Pass your own warning for any check you run before sending.

faq.q: Can I use it for messages that aren't email?
faq.a: Yes. Change the `title` and `labels`, and pass the recipients and send options you need. With no `attachments` and no `warning`, neither shows.
